subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: Source evidence shows the requested behavior is not implemented, but current docs/tests encode the opposite behavior and the change affects sandbox write-boundary expectations.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access, not no sandbox writes, and require a full mount/bridge/tool/docs update with regression proof.

options.title: Keep `none` read-only
options.body: Leave the security default as-is, close or reframe this as a docs/support issue, and point users to an explicit future writable-isolated mode if desired.

options.title: Fold into least-privilege bind design
options.body: Defer this exact semantic change and resolve it together with selective writable bind behavior tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access, not no sandbox writes, and require a full mount/bridge/tool/docs update with regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The central files and recent sandbox security history point most strongly to steipete for the product/security boundary decision.
